concepts.def: Allied conferences that agreed the division of Germany and Berlin into occupation zones, but exposed growing distrust between the USA and USSR.
America's pledge to support free peoples resisting communism, beginning with aid to Greece and Turkey and committing the USA to containment.
Stalin cut road and rail routes into West Berlin; the Western Allies supplied the city by airlift for almost a year until he backed down.
Thirteen-day standoff after the USA discovered Soviet missile sites on Cuba, ending when Khrushchev withdrew the missiles in return for American concessions.
Gorbachev's reforms and revolutions across Eastern Europe, including the fall of the Berlin Wall in 1989, ended the Cold War as the USSR dissolved in 1991.
The 2001 al-Qaeda attacks on the USA led to wars in Afghanistan from 2001 and Iraq in 2003, reshaping international relations after the Cold War.

walkthroughs.body_html:
International Relations 1945-2003 — a core area of GCSE History.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

International Relations 1945-2003 brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with International Relations 1945-2003.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: What did the Truman Doctrine of 1947 commit the USA to?
options: Containing the spread of communism by supporting countries under threat
Invading the Soviet Union
Withdrawing from European affairs
Sharing nuclear technology with the USSR

mcqs.q: How did the Western Allies respond to the Berlin Blockade of 1948-49?
options: They supplied West Berlin by air for almost a year until the blockade was lifted
They sent tanks through the Soviet checkpoints
They abandoned West Berlin to Soviet control
They built the Berlin Wall

mcqs.q: How was the Cuban Missile Crisis of 1962 resolved?
options: Khrushchev withdrew the missiles in return for a US pledge not to invade Cuba and the secret removal of US missiles from Turkey
The USA invaded Cuba and removed the missiles by force
The United Nations took over the government of Cuba
The USSR fired a warning missile at Florida

mcqs.q: Which event in November 1989 became the symbol of the end of the Cold War in Europe?
options: The fall of the Berlin Wall
The Cuban Missile Crisis
The launch of Sputnik
The Yalta Conference

mcqs.q: Did the Berlin Blockade lead to direct fighting between the superpowers?
options: The Berlin Blockade was a naval blockade of Germany's ports.
The Berlin Blockade ended when Allied troops fought their way into Berlin.
No - the Western Allies avoided armed confrontation by flying supplies into West Berlin for almost a year, until Stalin lifted the blockade in May 1949.
The Berlin Wall was built by the Americans to protect West Berlin.

mcqs.q: Why was the Berlin Wall built in 1961?
options: The Berlin Blockade was a naval blockade of Germany's ports.
The Berlin Wall was built by the Americans to protect West Berlin.
East Germany built it to stop the flood of its own citizens escaping to the West through West Berlin, which was draining skilled workers.
The Berlin Wall was built to keep Western invaders out of East Berlin.

mcqs.q: Did the Cold War officially end the night the Berlin Wall fell in 1989?
options: The Cold War ended when Germany joined the United Nations.
No - the Wall's fall was symbolic, but the Cold War ended through a process running to the dissolution of the USSR in December 1991.
The Berlin Blockade was a naval blockade of Germany's ports.
The Cold War ended on the night of 9 November 1989 when the Wall came down.
